name: Grobhäusern
summary: Historical German vying game, a poker ancestor where players bet through two deals to make the best 4-card combination.
rules_text: Played with 32-card piquet pack, 2-8 players. Ante pot. Phase 1: deal 2 cards each. Eldest must bet minimum. Clockwise each player may call by matching current max bet or fold and forfeit bet. Last caller may raise, starting new calling round. Continue until all active players have called with no new raise. Folded cards are shuffled with stock. Phase 2: each remaining player receives 2 more cards to have 4. Eldest, then dealer etc. in reverse order may raise to start calling rounds as before. When betting ends, showdown: best 4-card hand wins pot. Rank high to low: four of a kind, 4-card flush, three of a kind, 3-card flush, pair (meaning two same suit). Four of a kind / three of a kind tie broke by rank Ace high Ten low. Flush/pair ties by card-point total, then earlier seat wins. If no raise in phase 2, no showdown; all phase-1 folders must retroactively match stakes and pot carries over.
rating_reason: Clear vying game: bet then compare 4-card hands.
